clarifyingQuestions: Should reads inside a transaction see uncommitted writes?
Should a delete inside a transaction hide lower-layer values?
What exception should invalid commit or rollback raise?
followUps: Add conflict detection for concurrent clients.
Add snapshot isolation with versioned values.
Persist committed writes with a write-ahead log.
followUpGuide: For optimistic conflict detection, version every key identity, including deletions and absent-key observations. Record read versions and validate them atomically with publishing writes. Also decide how to detect write-write conflicts; deleting and recreating a key must not reset its version and hide an intervening change.

For snapshot isolation, assign a snapshot at begin and read the newest value or deletion visible to that snapshot, while giving local writes precedence. Check concurrent writes to the same keys at commit. Snapshot reads alone do not implement isolation, and snapshot isolation can still admit write skew across different keys.

For durability, log the entire outermost transaction with framing and a commit boundary, then flush the committed log to durable storage before acknowledging it or publishing base changes. Recovery replays only complete committed groups; raw set/delete records alone can replay half a transaction after a crash. Inner commits only merge local layers.
complexityAnalysis: - begin pushes an empty layer. Time: O(1) amortized. Space: O(1) for that layer. rollback logically pops one layer in O(1); freeing a Python dictionary with k entries takes O(k), excluding any additional value finalization.
- get probes layers newest to oldest, then base. Time: O(d + 1) average, where d is transaction depth. Space: O(1).
- set and delete update one map. Time: O(1) average. Space: O(1) per distinct key written in a layer. Total retained state is O(B + W + d), with B base entries and W entries across all layers.
- commit merges one layer with k distinct written keys. Time: O(k) average. Auxiliary iteration space: O(1); the parent or base may allocate O(k) new entries.
solutionGuide: Use a private tombstone sentinel for deletes. A real `None` value and a deleted value are different states.
return None if value is TOMBSTONE else value

target = self.layers[-1] if self.layers else self.base
